extracted.intended_audience: analysts, managers, and policymakers involved in Department of Defense / military medical treatment facility productivity measurement and Efficiency Review processes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed rubric for designing and evaluating productivity/performance measures for Department of Defense medical treatment facilities (MTFs), including a specific proposed indicator and supporting data/grouping rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid perverse or negative incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodology and the measure should avoid perverse or negative incentives for the entity measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures must not encourage behavior that reduces true performance (e.g., gaming workload counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulative potential of input variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should avoid manipulative potential of the input variables by interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose inputs that are hard for measured entities to alter fraudulently or strategically in order to inflate apparent performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available, identifiable, representative inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should rely on inputs that are available, easy to identify and representative of the actual inputs that go into the transformation process of the entity and result in the entity's products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer observable, routinely collected data rather than ad hoc or hard-to-collect variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of implementation and understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should be relatively simple to implement, use, and understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complexity reduces adoption and transparency; balance sophistication with operational usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce single-valued, understandable results
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should produce results that are single valued and understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an index or ratio that yields a single interpretable number (e.g., >=1 efficient, <1 inefficient) to aid decision makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology should be inexpensive and not labor intensive
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should incorporate a methodology that is inexpensive and not labor intensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid measures requiring excessive data collection or analysis costs relative to the value of the information produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate subjectivity in inputs where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: The input process should eliminate as much of the subjective as is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce reliance on judgment calls; prefer standardized definitions and automated or auditable data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid referencing quality within efficiency measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The efficiency measure should avoid any reference to quality of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efficiency indices should measure resource-to-output relationships; quality should be measured separately so that cost-cutting does not compromise care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate costs with performance (cost-per relationships)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be useful for resource planning, budgeting, and management, the measure should associate costs with performance; common relationships include cost per population, cost per output, and cost/percentage relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical/historical reasons indicate a measure probably should reflect cost per beneficiary or cost per patient episode. Advantages: (1) commonality across service measures; (2) not easily manipulated by the activity measured; (3) avoids perverse incentives. Disadvantages: (1) does not entirely explain demand drivers; (2) cost-per-output measures suffer from many surrogate labels and fewer advantages than cost-per-beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer cost-per-beneficiary as primary denominator
rubrics_metrics.description: Any measure developed probably should reflect a cost per beneficiary or cost per patient episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost-per-beneficiary avoids differences among varied service measures (outpatient visits, bed days) and is less easily manipulated; however, it may not fully explain demand drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cost/percentage (ratio) relationships to detect abnormalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost/percentage relationship can be considered the relationship of two costs and are useful to point out relationship changes over time for specific activities or functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ratios should be specifically related to intended measurement targets and used to identify anomalies rather than as sole performance indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of MTF data and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity of MTF data and definitions of variables/characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common data standards across facilities are necessary to make proxy measures comparable and to avoid misleading differences due to definition drift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of MTF policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity of most MTF policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, align policies across peer groups so policy differences do not confound productivity comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of cost center definition and full cost identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity of cost center definition, full cost identification, and recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent cost center definitions and full-cost accounting are required to compare facilities meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of non-direct patient care cost isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity of non-direct patient care cost isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolate indirect and overhead costs consistently so comparisons focus on direct patient care where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform full-cost transfer-pricing methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity of full cost transfer-pricing methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent transfer-pricing prevents cross-facility distortions when accounting for shared services or internal billings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capability to trace costs to patient groupings (DRGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity and capability to trace costs to actual groupings of patients receiving services (DRGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracing costs to diagnosis-related groups enhances case-mix adjustment and comparability of utilization intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer grouping must be objective (use polyethetic clustering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer grouping should be as objective as possible and the recommended approach is polyethetic clustering analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer grouping variables (size, expense, mission) should be selected to bring homogeneity to groupings; classification decisions should be made at a high level (e.g., OASD(HA)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer grouping variables (recommended set)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical variables for peer grouping include size of hospitals by number of beds, number of services offered, types of services offered, number of in-house teaching/residency programs, number of admissions, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these variables for linear regression or cluster analysis to form comparable peer groups; recognize changes of grouping materially affect workload weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select standard: actual output / expected output
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a basic standard of actual amounts of output divided by expected amounts of output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ratio yields a value of one for expected performance, less than one for inefficiency, greater than one for exceeding expectations; it permits time and cross-facility comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative model: total facility period costs / expected facility utilization
rubrics_metrics.description: A modified model relates total facility period costs to expected facility utilization producing an average cost per expected beneficiary utilization for the measured facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model is meaningful for decision makers comparing similar outpatient or inpatient clinics; it produces a single-valued average cost per expected beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure must incorporate four data elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure should incorporate four elements of data: (1) period facility total adjusted costs, (2) beneficiary groupings for demographic representation, (3) incidence rates of expected utilization, and (4) an adjustment factor for intensity of services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four elements feed the proposed indicator I = C'/U' (adjusted costs divided by expected adjusted utilization). Ensure each element is obtained/constructed consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total cost data guidance and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Total cost data element is to be obtained from internal sources that generate actual costs; to reduce variance, unit prices can be standardized for the period (e.g., averaged billet labor cost, geographic energy price per kWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inclusion of cost elements not controllable and not direct patient care for local cost centers. Where complexity exists, proxied cost elements might include labor, material, equipment, energy, and overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary grouping schema (use DEERS categories and age/sex breakdowns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group beneficiaries by common attributes (income, age, sex) and use DEERS-provided categories: active duty personnel, active duty dependents, retired personnel, retired dependents, survivors; age groupings and sex (male/female) are recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further subdivide by enlisted/officer and rank where useful. Use these groupings to calculate expected utilization B_j and incidence vectors A_j.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use incidence-rate adjustment factor for intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: The incidence rate adjustment factor reflects the intensity of resource allocation necessary for a given incidence rate of a specified event; adjustment factors can be adapted from references (e.g., California Relative Value Studies) or developed locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute incidence = (number of events during period) / (population exposed) and often multiply by 1000 (events per thousand). Consider DRGs as promising representation of utilization in the performance measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure should be adaptable and respect population/service heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure can be adapted to any level of the health services system and provides a methodology that respects differences of population, patient, health care services and activities, and product(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed measure permits comparison of expected to actual utilization patterns across comparable levels of activity and over time, aiding decision makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link measurement to incentive schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency Review program directives stress the need for relating the measurement, evaluation, and analysis of productivity to some incentive scheme that induces efficiency; an ideal measure would itself contain an incentive for efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design measures so they support reward/penalty mechanisms or management controls; measurement without credible incentives risks tokenism or cosmetic personnel reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement must evaluate the actual situation and be tailored to decision scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Before productivity improvement decisions are made, performance measurement should evaluate the actual situation; managers need information tailored to the specific scope of decision processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance measures should augment decision makers' understanding of cost center efficiency so that objective rewards and penalties, and corrective actions, can be applied appropriately.
